fullPassage:
Stress not only affects physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, making us even more likely to experience a drained brain.

(C) A number of studies have been done to reveal what happens in healthy people's brains when they go through something stressful. One study demonstrated a link between a smaller hippocampus and people who had experienced long-lasting stress.

(A) Why does this matter? This part of the brain helps you remain resilient in the face of stress and is involved in mood regulation. It also helps you to monitor the safety of your environment and store dangerous images in your long-term memory so you can avoid them in the future.

(B) It does all these things as part of its duties of regulating your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to turning signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' which can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or freeze.

questions.passage: Stress not only <u>affects</u> physical disease but also the very structure of our brains, <u>making</u> us even more likely to experience a <u>draining</u> brain. A number of studies <u>have</u> been done to reveal what happens.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ draining → drained: 뇌가 '소진된' 상태이므로 과거분사 drained가 적절. draining은 '소진시키는'(능동).
det.analysis:
✅ ① affects: 주어 Stress(단수) → affects 올바름
✅ ② making: 분사구문(결과) — making us ~
❌ ③ draining → drained: 뇌가 소진'된' 상태 → 과거분사
✅ ④ have: A number of studies(복수) → have
det.tip: drained(소진된: 수동/상태) vs draining(소진시키는: 능동)

questions.passage: A number of studies have been done to reveal <u>what</u> happens in healthy people's brains <u>when</u> they go through something stressful. One study <u>demonstrating</u> a link between a smaller hippocampus and people <u>who</u> had experienced long-lasting stress.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ demonstrating → demonstrated: 주어 One study의 동사가 필요. 현재분사만으로는 문장이 불완전.
det.analysis:
✅ ① what: 간접의문문 — reveal what happens
✅ ② when: 시간 부사절 접속사
❌ ③ demonstrating → demonstrated: 주절 동사 필요 (과거형)
✅ ④ who: 관계대명사 주격, people who had experienced
det.tip: 주어 + 동사(demonstrated) — 현재분사(demonstrating)는 동사 역할 불가

questions.passage: This part of the brain helps you <u>remain</u> resilient in the face of stress and is <u>involved</u> in mood regulation. It also helps you <u>to monitor</u> the safety of your environment and <u>storing</u> dangerous images in your long-term memory.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ storing → store: help + 목적어 + (to) 동사원형 구조에서 and 뒤에 병렬로 동사원형이 필요.
det.analysis:
✅ ① remain: help + 목적어 + 동사원형
✅ ② involved: be involved in = ~에 관여하다
✅ ③ to monitor: help + 목적어 + to부정사
❌ ④ storing → store: and로 to monitor와 병렬 → (to) store
det.tip: help + O + to V / V: helps you to monitor and store (병렬)

questions.passage: It does all these things as part of its duties of <u>regulating</u> your sympathetic and parasympathetic nervous systems. But chronic stress can confuse the hippocampus and lead to <u>turning</u> signals for cortisol 'on' instead of 'off,' <u>that</u> can trap you in a constant state of fight, flight, or <u>freeze</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ that → which: 콤마 뒤 계속적 용법에서는 which를 사용. that은 계속적 용법 불가.
det.analysis:
✅ ① regulating: of + 동명사 (duties of regulating)
✅ ② turning: lead to + 동명사 (lead to turning)
❌ ③ that → which: 콤마 + 관계대명사 = which (계속적 용법)

det.korean: ④ 'off' → 'on': 만성 스트레스는 코르티솔 신호를 끄는 대신 '켜'놓게 한다. 원문은 'on' instead of 'off'.
